This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let\[f(n) = \sum_{p<n}\frac{1}{n-p}.\]Is it true that\[\liminf f(n)=1\]and\[\limsup f(n)=\infty?\]Is it true that $f(n)=o(\log\log n)$ for all $n$?
#950: [Er77c,p.63]
number theory | 
primes
This function was considered by de Bruijn, Erdős, and Turán, who showed that\[\sum_{n<x}f(n)\sim \sum_{n<x}f(n)^2\sim x.\]They give no proofs, but a proof of the (harder) second claim is given by Gorodetsky here. The existence of some $c>0$ such that there are $\gg n^c/\log n$ many primes in $[n,n+n^c]$ implies that $\liminf f(n)>0$. 
Erdős writes that a 'weaker conjecture which is perhaps not quite inaccessible' is that, for every $\epsilon>0$, if $x$ is sufficiently large there exists $y<x$ such that\[\pi(x)< \pi(y)+\epsilon \pi(x-y).\](Compare this to [855].) He notes that if\[\pi(x)< \pi(y)+O\left(\frac{x-y}{\log x}\right)\]for all $y<x-(\log x)^C$ for some constant $C>0$ then $f(n)\ll \log\log\log n$.
The study of $f(p)$ is even harder, and Erdős could not prove that\[\sum_{p<x}f(p)^2\sim \pi(x).\]See also [1210].
Additional thanks to: Aron Bhalla

 I'm having trouble reconstructing the de Bruijn-Erdos-Turan claim $\sum_{n < x} f(n)^2 \sim x$ (which is not detailed in the reference given). Upper bound sieves can give a bound of the shape $\sum_{n < x} f(n)^2 \ll x$, but to get the asymptotic seems to require an understanding of the error term in the prime number theorem in almost all intervals of the form $[x, x+x^\theta]$ for $\theta$ close to zero, and at our current level of understanding this is only available on the density hypothesis (and hence on the Lindelof or Riemann hypothesis). 
In another direction, it seems likely that one can at least show that the lim sup will be infinite assuming the Hardy-Littlewood prime tuples conjecture, by working with suitable dense clusters of primes.

 $$\sum_{p\le x} f(p+1)^2 \sim 4 \pi(x).$$
The latter nevertheless does also not give any indication that the limsup should be infinity.
